en.topic: Term 1 review: voice, register and punctuation

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is written in the passive voice?
options: The window was broken by the ball.
questions.answer: The window was broken by the ball.
questions.hint: In the passive, the subject receives the action.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is written in the active voice?
options: The meal was cooked by the chef.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite in the passive voice by filling the gap: 'The dog chased the cat.' → 'The cat ___ by the dog.'
questions.hint: You need a form of 'to be' plus a past participle.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why might a writer choose the passive voice in a science report?
options: To focus on what happened rather than who did it
To make the writing sound chatty
questions.answer: To focus on what happened rather than who did it

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses the subjunctive correctly?
options: If I were taller, I could reach the shelf.
If I was taller, I could reach the shelf.
If I am taller, I could reach the shelf.
If I be taller, I could reach the shelf.
questions.answer: If I were taller, I could reach the shelf.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses the subjunctive?
options: The teacher insisted that every pupil be on time.
The teacher said every pupil is on time.
The teacher hopes pupils are on time.
questions.answer: The teacher insisted that every pupil be on time.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the most formal way to ask for information?
options: I would be grateful if you could send me the details.
Can you just tell me stuff?
questions.answer: I would be grateful if you could send me the details.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is the most formal replacement for 'get' in 'You can get a ticket at the door'?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a semi-colon correctly?
options: It was raining heavily; we stayed indoors.
It was raining; heavily we stayed indoors.
It was; raining heavily we stayed indoors.
It was raining heavily we; stayed indoors.
questions.answer: It was raining heavily; we stayed indoors.
questions.hint: A semi-colon joins two closely related main clauses.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a colon correctly to introduce a list?
options: You will need three things: a pencil, a ruler and a rubber.
You will need: three things a pencil, a ruler and a rubber.
You: will need three things, a pencil, a ruler and a rubber.
You will need three: things a pencil, a ruler and a rubber.
questions.answer: You will need three things: a pencil, a ruler and a rubber.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In which sentence are the dashes used for parenthesis?
options: My cousin – who lives in Wales – is visiting.
My cousin who – lives in Wales is – visiting.
My – cousin who lives in Wales is visiting –.
– My cousin who lives in Wales is visiting.
questions.answer: My cousin – who lives in Wales – is visiting.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which punctuation mark could replace the commas in this sentence without changing its meaning? 'The castle, built in 1200, still stands.'

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a semi-colon to separate items in a complex list?
options: We visited Paris, France; Rome, Italy; and Lisbon, Portugal.
We visited; Paris, Rome and Lisbon.
We visited Paris; France, Rome; Italy.
We; visited Paris, France, Rome, Italy.
questions.answer: We visited Paris, France; Rome, Italy; and Lisbon, Portugal.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Change this sentence into the active voice: 'The prize was won by Lena.' Write the new sentence.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite this informal sentence in a formal register: 'Hey, the trip's been cancelled 'cos of the rain, so don't bother coming.'
questions.hint: Think about removing contractions and slang.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one sentence that uses a colon to introduce an explanation, and one that uses a semi-colon to join two related clauses.

en_read.topic: Term 1 review: comparing genres and themes

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'retrieval' mean in reading?
options: Finding information that is stated in the text
questions.answer: Finding information that is stated in the text

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'inference' mean in reading?
options: Using clues in the text to work out something not directly stated
Copying a sentence from the text
Looking up a word in a dictionary
questions.answer: Using clues in the text to work out something not directly stated

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Maya slammed the door and threw her bag on the floor.' What can you infer about Maya?
options: She is excited about a party
questions.hint: Think about what her actions show.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'The streets were empty, the shops were boarded up and the wind howled.' What mood does this create?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a theme in a story?
options: A big idea or message the story explores
The name of the main character
The place where the story happens
questions.answer: A big idea or message the story explores

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Two stories show characters who keep trying after failing. Which theme do they share?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which feature is typical of a non-chronological report?
options: Subheadings and facts about a topic
questions.answer: Subheadings and facts about a topic

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which genre usually includes a detective, clues and a puzzle to solve?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which genre tells the true story of a person's life, written by someone else?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A story ends with the lesson 'Slow and steady wins the race.' Which genre is it most likely to be?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Leo's knees trembled as he stepped onto the stage.' Which word in the sentence best shows Leo is nervous?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'The old house had watched the village grow for two hundred years.' Which technique is used?
questions.hint: An object is given a human action.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a test, a question says 'Find and copy one word that…'. What should you do?
options: Copy the exact word from the text
Write the word in your own words
questions.answer: Copy the exact word from the text

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which question is a retrieval question?
options: In which city does the story take place?
Why do you think Ana felt proud?
How would you change the ending?
questions.answer: In which city does the story take place?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Think of two stories you read this term. Explain one theme they share and give an example from each.
questions.hint: Themes might be friendship, courage or belonging.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Sam glanced at the empty seat beside him and sighed.' What can you infer about how Sam feels? Use evidence from the sentence.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: begining → beginning; rythm → rhythm; temprature → temperature; noticable → noticeable; sinserely → sincerely
questions.text: At the begining of the concert, the hall was quiet. The drummer set a steady rythm and the temprature seemed to rise as people danced. It was a noticable change, and the effect on the crowd was amazing. We wrote to thank the band, signing the letter sinserely.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling of the word meaning "easy to see or notice" is correct?
questions.hint: Keep the 'e' to keep the 'c' soft.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words in this school-fair report.
questions.answer: responsable → responsible; stationary → stationery; desert → dessert; dramaticaly → dramatically; affect → effect
questions.text: Our class was responsable for the school fair. We bought new stationary for the posters and sold desert at the cake stall. The weather changed dramaticaly in the afternoon, but the rain had little affect on the fun. Everyone agreed it was a great success.
